sections.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of 4/3 n
sections.abstract: The paper proves that every thrackle on n≥4 vertices has at most floor(4(n−1)/3) edges, using a small-instance computer-assisted result and a discharging argument.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves m≤floor(4(n−1)/3) for every thrackleable graph with n≥4; the original m≤n conjecture remains unresolved.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite simple graphs drawn in the plane so every pair of edges meets exactly once, at a shared endpoint or a proper crossing.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an improved upper bound, not a proof or disproof of Conway's conjectured m≤n bound; the proof uses Pammer's computer-assisted verification for at most 12 vertices.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The introduction compares this bound with the previous 18/13(n−1) bound; the result spans three mathematical categories and combines a previously established finite verification with a new embedding/discharging argument.

sections.title: The Critical 2D KPZ Process
sections.abstract: The authors construct a non-Gaussian, distribution-valued critical two-dimensional KPZ process as a limit of centred Gaussian-directed-polymer log partition functions and of a renormalised logarithm of the critical stochastic heat flow.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove convergence in local negative Sobolev spaces, jointly at finitely many positive times and bounded continuous initial conditions, both from critically tuned Gaussian polymer partition functions and from regularised log-SHF; they also identify a log-log covariance singularity and Gaussian small-scale averages.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Two spatial dimensions, critical tuning, Gaussian disorder for the polymer approximation, and initial data in L-infinity(R²) intersect C(R²).
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is for the stated critical constructions, not a universality result for arbitrary disorder. The authors disclose extensive generative-AI assistance; the manuscript still needs independent expert scrutiny. The noise-mollified SHE limit is described by the authors as expected, with technical adaptations omitted.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper cross-lists probability and mathematical physics and states a concrete common limiting process for two regularisation routes, with additional local covariance and non-Gaussianity results in the main text.

sections.title: Positive sectional curvature on exotic spheres in infinitely many dimensions
sections.abstract: The author constructs exotic spheres with strictly positive sectional curvature in every dimension n≡3 mod 4, n≥11, except dimensions congruent to 255 modulo 256.
sections.claimed_result: For the specified family of S³-bundle quotient homotopy spheres, the author computes the Eells–Kuiper invariant and finds maps yielding nonzero invariant, which implies exotic smooth structure; the positive-curvature metric comes from the compatible-disk construction cited in the paper.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Spheres of dimension 4b+3 arising from the representation of S³ on R³⊕Hᵇ, for b≥2; the nonvanishing argument covers b not congruent to 63 mod 64.
sections.unique_caveat: The general theorem leaves the congruence class b≡63 mod 64 untreated; a computer calculation only reports additional dimensions in that class below 2^16.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The result gives an infinite family beyond the previously known high-dimensional examples described in the introduction; the paper links computation programs and outputs in a Zenodo archive.

sections.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in F_p^d for p=2,d=8 and p=11,d=3
sections.abstract: The authors prove the finite-field Fuglede conjecture in F₂⁸ and F₁₁³, and derive further structural results and reductions in F₂⁹.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show tiling and spectrality are equivalent for nonempty sets in F₂⁸ and F₁₁³; in F₂⁹ every tile is spectral, every spectral set has power-of-two size, and all spectral cardinalities except 64 are shown to tile.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite vector spaces over prime fields, with spectral meaning that the set admits an orthogonal character basis and tiles meaning it tiles by translation.
sections.unique_caveat: The dimension-nine argument leaves spectral cardinality 64 unresolved; the authors provide reductions rather than a full resolution there.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It settles two specific cases of a major tiling/spectral-set conjecture, pushes structural results into dimension nine, and supplies appendices describing exact computations and verification programs.

sections.title: Deep holes of full-length Reed–Solomon codes: uniform bounds and exact classifications
sections.abstract: The author classifies deep holes for specified interpolation-degree offsets over all finite fields, and proves uniform nonexistence/classification bounds for larger offsets under stated field-size conditions.
sections.claimed_result: For full-length RS_q(k) and interpolation degree k+m, all cases m=3,4,5,6,7 are classified over every finite field; for general m≥3, if √q≥12(m+1)log(2m+2), the author rules out deep holes when q is odd, or k≥3, or m is odd; if q>16(m+2)^4, the paper gives a complete classification at every admissible k.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Received words for the full-length Reed–Solomon code over a finite field; the classification depends on m, field size q, dimension k, and characteristic, with explicit characteristic-two exceptions at m=4,6.
sections.unique_caveat: The uniform bounds require large fields, and the exact exceptional families in small characteristic are part of the statement; the result does not erase those cases.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper cross-lists coding theory, combinatorics, and number theory; it gives exact cases for offsets 3–7 and provides certificates and deterministic verification programs for remaining finite cases.

sections.title: Upper tail large deviations of regular subgraph counts in sparse random regular graphs
sections.abstract: The authors determine upper-tail large-deviation rates for regular-subgraph counts in sparse random regular graphs across two regimes and describe the conditioned graph structure in key cases.
sections.claimed_result: For connected Δ-regular H, the authors obtain speeds and rate functions for copies of H in G_n^d when p=d/n is small and np^(Δ/2)≫(log n)^(1/(v_H−2)); for Δ≥3 these match Erdős–Rényi, while for cycles the rate function differs. They also establish matching Erdős–Rényi rates in a complementary sparse regime for strictly balanced graphs.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Random d-regular graphs, sparse edge density, and the explicit asymptotic regimes in the abstract; conditioned-structure claims concern the corresponding upper-tail events.
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusions are regime-specific; cycle counts behave differently from the Δ≥3 case, and the paper does not claim one rate formula across all densities.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper bridges probability and graph combinatorics, distinguishes the cycle case from higher-degree regular patterns, and identifies typical structures under the rare event rather than giving only a rate.

sections.title: A new lower bound for the sixth Schur number: S(6)≥537
sections.abstract: The authors give an explicit partition of {1,…,537} into six sum-free sets, improving the known lower bound for the sixth Schur number by one.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish S(6)≥537 and use known recursive constructions to obtain improved lower bounds S(8)≥5,372, S(11)≥204,208, S(13)≥2,042,082, and R₆(3)≥539.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Schur numbers concern partitions of initial positive integers into sum-free color classes; the paper supplies explicit finite partitions rather than an exact value for S(6).
sections.unique_caveat: This is a lower-bound improvement, not a determination of the sixth Schur number; the reported searches do not establish that the listed partitions exhaust all possibilities.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper improves a published benchmark dating to 2000, reports 131 inequivalent partitions, and includes the explicit witness data and a verification script.

sections.title: An explicit elementary proof of no Landau–Siegel zeros
sections.abstract: The author claims an explicit lower bound (1−β)log q>1/100 for every real zero β of a primitive quadratic Dirichlet L-function of conductor q≥3.
sections.claimed_result: The author asserts that every real zero β in (0,1) for every primitive quadratic Dirichlet character χ of conductor q≥3 satisfies (1−β)log q>0.01.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Real zeros of Dirichlet L(s,χ) for primitive quadratic characters, with no conductor exception beyond q≥3 according to the abstract.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an exceptionally strong, unrefereed preprint claim with no journal reference in the arXiv record; neither its proof nor independent expert validation was checked here, so it should not be treated as established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The stated uniform, explicit zero-free claim would be highly consequential if correct, so it is included as a high-interest claim to scrutinize; the evidence is the precise theorem statement, not observed attention or independent confirmation.
